lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. There's a draw past the Halvorsen road where I put my crew in the ground last summer. Olle, Nils and the Dutchman. I never said the words over them. I was too busy being shot.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then we'll go and say them.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: I'll bring the hymnal. I can't read it, but it helps to hold it.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: That's new. That wire. That wasn't there.

lines.speaker: rider
lines.line: Syndicate land, old man. Says so on the sign. Your friends are trespassing, and so are you.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: They are dead. They are not trespassing. They are only lying down.

lines.speaker: rider
lines.line: Then they won't mind the fence.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Hap. Hold the horses. I'm going to cut the wire.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: There. There, boys. Nobody fences you in now. Rest easy.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Sing, Hap. Sing to them through the wire. Let these men listen.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Den stora vita skaran... I don't know the English. The tune is the same in heaven, I think.

lines.speaker: rider
lines.line: Go on, old man. Finish it. We'll wait.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Thank you, Mrs. Caddell. They were good boys. Olle cheated at cards, but kindly.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Now they have a Swede singing over them. That's the worst thing that ever happened to them, and they've been shot.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've heard worse singing, Hap. Not much worse. But some.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Cher, a man of Orrin Tate's came by camp tonight while you were out. Tate holds my marker. Forty dollars and interest, and the interest has teeth.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: There's a night boat from the Port Linden pier at eleven. I can be on it. You'd never have to see Tate's men around the fire again.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You'll want company to the pier, then.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: I always want company. I never ask for it. That's the difference between me and a dog.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.line: Arceneaux! Mr. Tate figured you'd come for the boat.

lines.speaker: tate
lines.line: Delphine. You've grown thin on honest living. Forty dollars, or the boat goes without you, one way or the other.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Here's your forty. Count it twice. You'll want to remember the feeling.

lines.speaker: tate
lines.line: Paid in full. You keep expensive friends, Delphine.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Nobody's ever paid my way before. Now I'll have to stay. I'd be in your debt, and I don't run out on a debt. Not that kind.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Here's a ticket for the boat, Del. Paid. Go if you want. I won't think less of you.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: You'd let me go. Just like that.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Then I'm staying. A woman doesn't run from the only person who'd let her. Tate, you'll get your forty when I win it off you, fair.

lines.speaker: tate
lines.line: Then you'll get nothing. Boys.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: That's the trouble with staying, cher. Everyone knows where to find you.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That's also the good of it.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: A letter. From Philadelphia. From the widow of the man I killed, if you'll forgive my precision.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Mrs. Agnes Whitcomb. She writes that she has forgiven me. Fourteen years. I'd rather she'd cursed me. I know what to do with a curse.

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: Doctor! Señora! A wagon went over at the wells, on the teamster. His legs. Please, quickly!

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: My bag. My bag, Caddell, and your fastest horse.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Hold him. Hold him still, and talk to him. Anything. Tell him about your husband.

lines.speaker: teamster
lines.line: Am I going to lose them, Doc? I've got a route. I've got a wife.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: You'll keep the left. The right I'll argue with. Now bite this, and think of your wife.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: We were late. The leg's gone. He'll live. That will have to be enough for him, and for me.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Both legs, and him cursing like a sailor. My hands didn't shake. Not once. Did you notice?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I noticed.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Now. The letter. Tell me what to do with it. I find I can't decide, which is new.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Answer it. Tell her about today. Tell her you set a man's leg in the dirt with steady hands.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: She forgave the drunk. I'll write and introduce her to the doctor. I think she'd like him better. I'm beginning to.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Burn it. You don't owe her your absolution. You owe it to the man in the cantina with the broken legs.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: Ashes, then. Philadelphia always did burn well.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. Amos Pike, the foreman at Thornwood, he's still got Chance. My colt. I raised him from a foal on skimmed milk and he's the only thing I ever owned.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Pike says the colt's camp property, for the board I ate. I worked fourteen hours a day for that board.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You want to go and get him.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Tonight. There's no moon. I know where the dogs sleep.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Crouch low, stay behind me, and if I say run, you run. Not toward the shooting. Away from it.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Chance. Chance, it's me. Easy now. You got fat. They fed you better than me.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Here's fifteen dollars on the gatepost, under a stone. Pike will find it in the morning. Now he can't call it stealing.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: He doesn't deserve fifteen cents.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: No. But you deserve to own your horse clean.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Take him. They owe you three years of wages. That's worth one colt.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: That's what I said! That's exactly what I said!

lines.speaker: pike
lines.line: Who's at the corral? Pruitt, is that you? Thief! Get the dogs up!

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: He's mine. He's really mine. I'm going to teach him to rein like your mare.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I'll do it like you did, when I'm grown. Exactly like you did. You'll see.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That's what I'm afraid of, Billy.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: There's a cavalry captain at the Coldwater livery asking for me by my old name. Thorne. I scouted for him in ninety. He has a job.

lines.speaker: thorne
lines.line: Kehoe. A family left the Pine Ridge agency for the winter hunting ground without a pass. Old man, women, children. I need them found before the snow does it.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Before the snow does it. That's a kind way to put it, Captain.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Come with me, Ruth. I'll find them. I'd rather it was me than his Crow scouts. After that, I don't know.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Pony tracks, unshod, and a travois. They're going up the north fork. Slowly. Someone's sick.

lines.speaker: elder
lines.line: We are going where my father hunted. That is all. My grandson has a cough. The agency beef was green.

lines.speaker: mother
lines.line: Are you the soldiers?

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: No. We're the ones ahead of the soldiers. Take this meat. Keep north of the lake.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'll tell Thorne they went down the south canyon toward the railroad. It's a lie he'll believe because he wants to.

lines.speaker: thorne
lines.line: South. Toward the line. Well. That's that, then. Obliged, ma'am.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It's your fight, Joseph. Tell him what you want to tell him.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: I found them, Captain. I won't tell you where. I saw what happened at Wounded Knee. I'll not carry another family to it.

lines.speaker: thorne
lines.line: You'll never trade a horse to the army again, Kehoe. I'll see to it.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: The army never paid on time anyway.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: You let me say it myself. Most people would have said it for me, and been proud of how well they said it.
